sources.title: Hawaiian Islands National Wildlife Refuge, About Us
sources.source_date: Page did not expose a publication or revision date in the inspected content.
sources.license: U.S. federal agency page. No page-specific reuse license was displayed; no page bytes copied into this packet.

inspected_facts: FWS describes Gardner Pinnacles as two volcanic-rock pinnacles between French Frigate Shoals and Maro Reef.
FWS describes the island as five acres and as the smallest land area in the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands.
FWS identifies extensive underwater shelves separately from the island's dry-land area.

The refuge history states that President Theodore Roosevelt set aside the Northwestern Hawaiian chain (except Midway Atoll) as the Hawaiian Islands Reservation on 1909-02-03; the page identifies its refuge conservation role.
sources.method: Read the Gardner-specific section and refuge-history text on the official refuge page. FWS statements support named feature, broad dry-land scale and administrative conservation context, not a surveyed modern shoreline or political-sovereignty history.

subject_assessments.name: Gardner Pinnacles
subject_assessments.role: One named whole dry-land territory covering the Gardner Pinnacles feature; do not split by source polygon, shoreline ring, or individual rock without an independently defined territorial subject.

accounting.associated_named_dry_land_omitted_by_thi: No omitted associated feature identified within the issue's supplied source query. Query is local and cannot prove no remote or sub-resolution dry land exists.

subject_assessments.assessment: The retained OSM snapshot contains three closed coastline ways tagged natural=coastline and place=islet, with 50 node references (47 unique nodes) in total. The preserved extracted MultiPolygon contains three polygons, one exterior ring each, matching the three supplied way IDs. FWS independently describes the named feature as two volcanic pinnacles and a five-acre island. OSM's three shoreline components versus FWS's two pinnacles is a scale/feature-count difference, not grounds for inventing a third named location; the packet cannot establish whether each OSM component maps one-to-one to the two exposed pinnacle masses.
subject_assessments.settlement_assessment: No permanent settlement is evidenced in the inspected FWS feature account or the target OSM coastline ways. The OSM ways are physical coastline features and carry no name or settlement tags. This limited evidence does not establish historical non-habitation; historical settlement remains outside this geography packet and unresolved.
subject_assessments.source_coverage_limit: Bounding-box response contains four ways total (three target coastline ways and one other way), but it is not a complete regional inventory, bathymetric source, tidal datum study or sub-meter-independent shoreline survey. Shoreline completeness at high/low tide and omitted emergent rocks remain unresolved.
subject_assessments.recommended_treatment: Retain one location and the full three-ring source geometry as the dated 2026 source-backed representation. Do not enlarge it using underwater shelves, reef, bathymetry, political claims or administrative extent. Keep modern coverage/shoreline-completeness review open. No hierarchy or geometry change proposed.

The finite OSM bbox plus FWS narrative cannot certify all tiny/submerged-at-high-tide features or complete regional shoreline coverage.
